item.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
item.description: Brazil's opposition party accepts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: In Nairobi, a city prone to floods, workers in the "Green Army" are making preparations to prevent disaster when El Niño arrives.

item.title: Democrats have a midterm edge, poll shows. And, Israelis vote in high-stakes election
item.description: Democrats are still holding a slight edge with Election Day a week away, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. And, Israelis are casting their votes in an election that could change leadership.

item.title: Local ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump starts in southern Ukraine
item.description: A localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, as missile attacks resumed in Kyiv.

item.title: Australian judge rejects prisoner's human rights challenge to Vegemite ban
item.description: Andre McKechnie, 55, is serving a life sentence for murder. He took his battle for the salty, sticky, black-brown byproduct of brewing beer to the court last year. He argued being refused Vegemite breached the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act.

item.title: Russia says it will open humanitarian corridor to Ukrainian town
item.description: Russia says it will open a humanitarian corridor to the occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, where people have been eating weeds and pickles to survive while trapped by minefields, shelling and drones.

item.title: 'The smell of freedom': Serbia's student movement celebrates election triumph
item.description: A political earthquake has occurred in Serbia as a student-backed movement wins the parliamentary election, ending more than a decade of dominance by a Moscow-backed populist leader.
